_about: The dashboard To-Do feed. Refreshed at every Rule 9 checkpoint alongside the session handoff — this is the handoff distilled into plain language for the 📋 button on every tab. Split For Sam (curation / decisions only a human makes) and For Fable (engineering, the next session picks up).
_status: Three things you reported on the map are fixed. The drag that would not take was not about the second drag at all — repeating it eight times in a row all worked. It is about where you aim. When you open a course, the college courses under it fan out as little stars, and those stars drift over the neighbouring circles; the map was reading a drop as a click on the nearest star, which belonged to the course you were dragging FROM, so it answered "that course is already there" in a line at the very bottom of the window where nobody looks. Six circles on your screen were covered that way. Now a drop only ever lands on a circle, and while you are carrying a course the map draws a ring around where it will land and writes the name beside it, so you can see it before you let go. The duplicated skills are gone: colleges spell the same skill two ways — flux cored and flux-cored, process and processes — and each spelling was counted as its own skill. Across the whole reference that was 1,044 doubled-up rows; there are none now, and the row shows whichever spelling the most colleges wrote. You can also add a skill or remove one on the outline, staged in your browser like the title and subject beside it — nothing is written from that page. Merged courses no longer show as a white block on the dark map. Two things we found while looking: a course outline opened from a link showed no college courses at all, and the accessibility checker was reporting ten phantom problems inside a collapsed section. Both fixed. Still first in the queue and still unbuilt: the two CPL views you asked for, sketch first.

items.text: Eight calls are waiting on one page — the CPL views you asked to see sketched, the folded skill list you asked to check, and who signs a curate edit once it starts writing. Reply on the sheet itself; the chips save to it and the next session reads them. https://claude.ai/code/artifact/a7d53d9c-7031-4612-82e3-7905810c060e — and read item 1 before item 2: measuring from MAP's own credit funnel instead of the map's own copy changed the answer. Only 4.3% of MAP's CPL rows name a receiving course, which is the ceiling on anything the map can draw; and 'where they differ college to college' comes to four cases, not the pattern either of us expected.

You asked for a magic phrase people type before they can move a course, shifting to a team phrase later. That would be the first time anything is written from the map, which today writes nothing at all — so it goes through Governance and the privacy review before it ships rather than after. Say the word and it gets scoped.

Your ruling on where skill statements come from unblocked the course outline's skills layer — published agency standards are the text of record, an ACE exhibit fills a gap they leave, the MAP team overrides either, and a genuine conflict shows both side by side. But we hold none of that text: of 1,987 credentials classified, 64 of them welding, not one carries a skill field. So this is now a fetching problem, not a decision. The question for you is which published standard to start with — an AWS welding certification was the pilot.

Build the two sketches Sam asked for before any code: the CPL vs Course/Discipline toggle and the show-articulations toggle, together, since he called them linked. The absence rule is already ruled — light only what carries a number, mark nothing else.

Half of this shipped. The confirmation sentence no longer claims the move is 'recorded below the map' when you are in full-screen SkyView, where that panel is not drawn at all — it now says it is staged in your browser and counts how many moves you have made. What is still missing is the mark on the course itself: after you move one, its own dot and its row say nothing about being staged rather than saved.

The legend's 'unified' is the only entry with no explanation — stand-alone course, noncredit and college course each carry one. You said a note on Unified would be fine, so that is the fix, in the style already there. Hovers explaining M-ID, C-ID and CCN go with it.

The course outline still has an empty layer waiting for credit-for-prior-learning: the MAP exhibits and military credit recommendations that could award each course. It is no longer blocked on a decision — that was answered — it is blocked on holding the text at all.

Decision packs still only exist for 5 of the 159 disciplines because they are baked into the page. Fetching them per discipline the way the course descriptions already are is the bottleneck behind several of the remaining asks.
